title: Choose the visual world
question: Safer hand: three grounded directions from the conventional end, plus the category standard. No roll this round — you pick.

options.label: Le décompte détaillé
options.lineage: the payslip and the accountant's columnar pad, deracinated from money
options.thesis: Every line declares where it came from, the reader's own figure is marked as theirs, and the total is ruled off.
options.viewport: A boxed header carrying the rule and its question, then the computation as lines in labelled columns — quantity, factor, emissions — with each emission factor's source cited on the line that uses it, the reader's own input marked as theirs, and the total on a heavy rule at the foot beside its normalised twin.
options.risk: A table of figures with a total is the most familiar shape in the world, and familiarity is what makes it disappear — the notation has to earn attention somewhere, and the citation column is where it must.

options.label: L’étiquette nutritionnelle
options.thesis: The same computation declared in two contexts side by side, with a reference scale to say whether the number is a lot.
options.viewport: A boxed declaration panel with two columns — per festivalier and per day against the whole event — the postes listed under it with a “dont” nest, thick rules separating declared values from the reference scale, and the emission factor of each line printed beneath it in small type.
options.risk: Carries two contexts better than anything else here, but a label is a fixed panel: it has no way to show a chain six references deep without becoming a table again.

options.label: La fiche service-public.fr
options.lineage: the French government fiche and the gov.uk guidance page
options.thesis: The document is a frame the state already taught every reader how to use, and the computation is set inside it as a plain table.
options.viewport: An “En bref” card answering the reader's question in three lines, an anchor menu down the side, the computation set as a plain table under a plain heading, and the emission factors' sources gathered into “Textes de référence” at the foot.
options.risk: The cleanest frame on the table and the weakest carrier of the mechanism — government web has never had to render a nested computation, so it explains figures in prose, which is the failure this product exists to refuse.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Sidebar of rule names, breadcrumb, the rule's title and prose, then the computation as an indented tree of labelled boxes — executed impeccably, benchmarked against gov.uk, the ADEME Base Empreinte documentation, and mon-entreprise's current v1 rule page.
canonCard.viewport: A left rail listing rules, the rule's title and description, and under it a bordered box holding an indented tree of mechanism labels in grey small caps with values right-aligned.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design. mon-entreprise already ships it, and the brief ruled out the shape.
